question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cotangent-cosecant identity 

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡x-{cot}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity

$$
{coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{x{coth}^{2}⁡x+x{csch}^{2}⁡x}{{coth}^{4}⁡x-{csch}^{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{x({coth}^{2}⁡x+{csch}^{2}⁡x)}{({coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x)({coth}^{2}⁡x+{csch}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{x}{({coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{x}{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{1}^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
